title: Close Enough to Hear Him
style: Adult contemporary jazz-pop with a relaxed swing-leaning midtempo groove; piano and Rhodes trade warm extended chords, brushed kit and upright bass keep a supple pulse, with restrained saxophone replies between vocal phrases. A conversational New England female lead carries detailed, narrative verses, opening into a memorable, gently rising chorus; add soft layered harmonies late, then resolve with a small piano-and-sax outro. Intimate, clear mix with warm saturation, natural room depth, and the voice forward.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Gabriele was the last one I expected
To ask me how my father was
I’m still deciding, did Thomas send her
Or did she call because he wouldn’t?
My money’s on Gabriele, anyway
She sounded like she’d missed his name
Twice I thought she had a story of her own
Then let the quiet close again

[Pre-Chorus]
Vicky called, and Bogotá called
A couple clients checked in, too
Libardo and Thomas would care
Though neither one would make the call
The rest had lives already full
Fair enough, I tell myself

[Chorus]
He was getting better, bit by bit
I watched the good hand find its work
Bed to chair, and back again
I kept his heels from taking hurt
No grand turn, no sudden change
Just one more day, then one more week
He was getting better, and I stayed
Close enough to hear him breathe

[Verse 2]
By Columbus Day, Maureen could take over
A home-care nurse would lend a hand
María Teresa confirmed my leave
So I knew I could afford the plan
I took the afternoon to Providence
To have coffee with my mother there
She’d been on her own since COVID took him
Six years now, and still she’s everywhere

[Verse 3]
Accounting, book club, friends who dance
I can’t keep all their names in line
She seemed less tired after the grief passed
And happier, which felt like a sign
I wondered if the steps from Colombia
Might help me meet her on the floor
We ran out of time before I found out
I hugged her longer at the door

[Chorus]
He was getting better, bit by bit
I watched the good hand find its work
Bed to chair, and back again
I kept his heels from taking hurt
No grand turn, no sudden change
Just one more day, then one more week
He was getting better, and I stayed
Close enough to hear him breathe

[Verse 4]
I don’t think I’d held on that long
Since I was eleven, maybe twelve
I still expect her birthday call
And I’ll call hers, the way we always have
Then Worcester, one last week with Dad
And Claire went straight into the news
Thomas had shut himself at Villa Jaguar
Pilar and Vicky there, but out of reach

[Pre-Chorus]
I’d talked to Vicky, wasn’t worried
Claire was, and made the call
Fernando would meet me at the airport
Fly me straight to Punta Espada

[Chorus]
He was getting better, bit by bit
I’d done what I could, and stayed
Now there’s a plane to catch from Worcester
And a long way left to make
No grand turn, no final word
Just care that traveled where it could
He was getting better, and I’m going
Because she asked me to

[Outro]
The refund came through, Logan to El Dorado
Via Salvador, the plan I had
Now I’m counting on Fernando
At Worcester Regional, like an Uber with wings
On Claire’s dime
